newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end flat ahead of Congress vote.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end flat ahead of Congress vote.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to slightly softer on Tuesday ahead of Congress' debate on the government's economic measures.
"The market is positioned for the passage through Congress of the measures," said a trader at a large foreign bank.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.05 to 117.30. Argentina's FRB due 2005 was flat at 80-1/2.
Traders reported some profit-taking during the session, but the foreign bank trader said the market was well supported around current levels.
Another trader reported the market showed its strength this session considering it did not fall in the face of large declines of U.S. Treasuries.

Ever since new Economy Minister Roque Fernandez first disclosed a larger-than-expected budget deficit this year, the market has fretted over the implementation of the government's tax raising measures aimed at plugging that deficit because of reluctance in Congress.
But "we expect that Congress will pass the government's measures more or less as the government wants them," said the second trader.

Separately, Argentina reportedly agreed in principle with the International Monetary Fund on a $5.0 billion budget deficit this year. Fernandez has warned that without the measures he proposes the deficit could rise to $6.6 billion.
In the money markets, one day call money rates fell to 7.30 percent from 7.70 percent.
